1: The person who delights in God's law is like a tree planted by a stream. The wicked are like chaff blown by the wind.
The doorway to the whole Psalter: there are two roads, and they end differently.
2: Nations plot against God and his anointed. God laughs and says to his king, "You are my Son; today I have begotten you."
The New Testament reads this of Christ.
3: David, fleeing his son Absalom, is surrounded by enemies. He lies down, sleeps and wakes, because the Lord sustains him.
Trust lets a hunted man sleep.
4: "When I called, the God of my justice heard me." In peace I will lie down and sleep.
5: "In the morning you hear my voice." God takes no pleasure in wickedness; lead me in your justice.
Starting the day by turning to God.
6: "Lord, do not rebuke me in your anger." My bed is soaked with tears. The Lord has heard my weeping.
The first of the seven penitential psalms.
7: Falsely accused, the psalmist appeals to God, who tests hearts.
Evil falls into the pit it digs.
8: "What is man that you are mindful of him?" Yet you have crowned him with glory and put all things under his feet.
Human dignity is God's gift. Hebrews applies it to Christ.
9: Thanks for God's justice, then a plea: why do you stand far off while the wicked hunt the poor? (Modern Bibles split this into Psalms 9 and 10.)
God does not forget the cry of the poor.
10: In the Lord I take refuge
Friends say, "Flee like a bird to the mountains." The psalmist stays: the Lord is in his holy temple.
Trust when the foundations seem destroyed.
11: Everyone speaks with flattering lips. The words of the Lord are pure, like silver refined seven times.
God's word can be trusted when human words cannot.
12: "How long will you forget me?" asked four times, then, "I have trusted in your mercy."
A model for praying through a long wait.
13: The fool says there is no God
God looks down for anyone who seeks him and finds all have turned aside.
Paul quotes this to show that all have sinned.
14: The one who walks blamelessly, speaks truth, does no wrong to his neighbour and keeps his word.
15: You will not abandon me to the grave
"The Lord is my portion." My body rests in hope, for you will not let your holy one see corruption.
Peter quotes this of Christ's resurrection.
16: Keep me as the apple of your eye
An innocent man asks protection. "Hide me in the shadow of your wings."
"When I awake, I shall be satisfied with seeing your face."
17: David's great song of thanks after God rescued him from all his enemies.
God is described with nine images of strength.
18: Sky and sun speak without words. The law of the Lord is perfect, sweeter than honey.
Creation and Scripture both reveal God.
19: A prayer for the king before battle
"May the Lord answer you in the day of trouble." Some trust in chariots; we trust in the name of the Lord.
20: The king rejoices in God's strength. God has given him his heart's desire.
21: My God, why have you forsaken me?
A just man is mocked; his hands and feet are pierced; they cast lots for his clothing. Then he praises God in the assembly.
Jesus prays this on the cross. It ends in triumph. (Psalm 22 in modern Bibles.)
22: "I shall not want." He leads me beside still waters. Even in the valley of the shadow of death I fear no evil. He prepares a table before me.
The best loved of all psalms. (Psalm 23 in modern Bibles.)
23: The earth is the Lord's. Who may climb his mountain? The clean of hand and pure of heart. "Lift up your gates, that the King of glory may enter."
Used in Advent, as the Church waits for the King.
24: "To you I lift up my soul." Do not remember the sins of my youth. Teach me your way.
A humble prayer for guidance and forgiveness.
25: I wash my hands in innocence
The psalmist asks God to test his heart, and says he loves the house where God dwells.
The priest once prayed this while washing his hands at Mass.
26: "Whom shall I fear?" One thing I ask: to dwell in the house of the Lord. "Wait for the Lord; be strong."
Confidence, and the desire to see God's face.
27: The Lord is my strength and shield
A cry not to be silent turns to thanks: he has heard my voice.
Prayer often ends in gratitude before the answer is visible.
28: God's voice thunders over the waters, breaks the cedars, shakes the desert.
"The Lord will bless his people with peace."
29: "You have lifted me up." Weeping lasts the night; joy comes at dawn. You turned my mourning into dancing.
Thanks after recovery from near death.
30: "In you, Lord, I have hoped." Into your hands I commend my spirit. My times are in your hand.
Jesus' last words on the cross come from here.
31: While I kept silent, my bones wasted. I confessed, and you forgave the guilt of my sin.
The second penitential psalm: the relief of confession.
32: By the word of the Lord the heavens were made. The Lord's plan stands for ever; his eye is on those who fear him.
Praise of God as Creator and Lord of history.
33: "I will bless the Lord at all times." Taste and see that the Lord is good. He is close to the broken-hearted.
34: Attacked without cause by people he had prayed for, the psalmist asks God to defend him.
"They hated me without cause," which Jesus applies to himself.
35: In your light we see light
The sinner has no fear of God. But God's mercy reaches to the heavens. "With you is the fountain of life."
God as the source of all life and light.
36: They fade like grass. Trust in the Lord and do good. The meek shall inherit the land.
Jesus quotes it in the Beatitudes. The psalm answers envy with patience.
37: "There is no health in my flesh because of my sin." Friends stand far off. "Do not forsake me."
38: The psalmist tries to stay silent and cannot. "Lord, let me know my end." Every man is but a breath.
39: "I waited for the Lord, and he heard my cry. Sacrifice you did not desire; then I said, Behold, I come to do your will."
Hebrews puts these words on Christ's lips.
40: Blessed is he who cares for the poor
A sick man is betrayed even by the friend who ate his bread.
Jesus applies the betrayal to Judas.
41: As the deer longs for water
"My soul thirsts for the living God." Why are you cast down, my soul? Hope in God.
The soul's thirst for God, sung at the Easter Vigil.
42: "Judge me, O God." Let your light lead me to your holy mountain and your altar.
Once prayed at the foot of the altar at the start of Mass.
43: Why do you hide your face?
Our fathers told us what you did. Now we are defeated and scattered, though we have not forgotten you.
"For your sake we are slain all the day long," which Paul quotes.
44: The king is the fairest of men, anointed with the oil of gladness. The queen stands at his right hand in gold.
Read of Christ and his Church, and of Our Lady.
45: "We will not fear though the earth be moved." "Be still, and know that I am God."
Calm confidence while the world shakes.
46: God is king of all the earth
"Clap your hands, all peoples." God has gone up with a shout.
47: Great is the Lord in his holy mountain. Kings saw it and fled.
48: Rich and poor alike die and take nothing with them. But God will redeem my soul from the grave.
Do not be awed by the rich.
49: God summons his people: I do not need your bulls. "Offer to God a sacrifice of praise."
Worship is thanksgiving and an upright life.
50: Have mercy on me, O God
David's prayer after his sin with Bathsheba: "Wash me. Against you I have sinned. Create in me a clean heart."
The Miserere, the greatest prayer of repentance, prayed every Friday morning. (Psalm 51 in modern Bibles.)
51: Why boast of evil, you who love lies? God will uproot you. I am like a green olive tree in God's house.
52: The fool says there is no God. (Almost the same as Psalm 13.)
Without God, people devour one another.
53: Betrayed to Saul, David prays, "God is my helper."
54: "Oh that I had wings like a dove!" It was not an enemy but my companion.
"Cast your care upon the Lord, and he will sustain you."
55: "When I am afraid, I put my trust in you." You have counted my tears.
God keeps a record of every sorrow.
56: In the shadow of your wings
Hiding in a cave from Saul, David sings, "My heart is ready. Awake, my soul!"
Praise in the middle of danger.
57: Do you rulers judge rightly? They are deaf like a snake that will not hear the charmer.
"Truly there is a God who judges on earth."
58: Enemies prowl like dogs around the city at night. "I will sing of your strength in the morning."
59: "You have rejected us." Give us help against the enemy.
60: "From the ends of the earth I cry to you. Lead me to the rock that is higher than I."
God is a tower of strength.
61: "My soul rests in God alone." If riches increase, do not set your heart on them.
Only God is a solid foundation.
62: "O God, you are my God; at dawn I seek you. Your love is better than life."
The classic morning psalm of longing for God.
63: Enemies sharpen their tongues like swords. God shoots his own arrow.
God turns slander back on itself.
64: "To you all flesh will come." You visit the earth and water it; the valleys shout for joy.
Thanks for forgiveness and for the fruits of the earth.
65: "Shout with joy to God, all the earth." He tested us like silver and brought us through fire and water.
66: "May God be gracious to us and bless us, that your way be known on earth."
A missionary prayer: blessing is meant to spread.
67: A triumphal procession: God, father of orphans and defender of widows, marches before his people.
Paul applies "he ascended on high" to Christ.
68: The waters have reached my neck
"I am sinking in deep mire." Zeal for your house consumes me. They gave me vinegar to drink.
The Gospels see this fulfilled in the Passion.
69: O God, come to my aid
"O Lord, make haste to help me."
These words open each hour of the Divine Office.
70: Do not cast me off in old age
"You have been my hope from my youth." Even when I am old and grey, do not forsake me.
71: The king of justice and peace
"May he defend the poor. May he rule from sea to sea." Kings will bring him gifts.
Read on the Epiphany of Christ.
72: "My feet had almost slipped," envying the arrogant. "Until I went into the sanctuary of God." Whom have I in heaven but you?
The answer to envy is God himself.
73: Enemies have smashed and burned the Temple. "Why, O God, have you cast us off?"
A prayer for the Church in times of ruin.
74: "He brings one down and lifts up another."
75: "In Judah God is known." He broke the weapons of war.
Even human anger ends up serving God's praise.
76: Has God forgotten to be gracious?
In the night I cannot sleep. Then: "I will remember the works of the Lord."
Memory of God's deeds heals despair.
77: A long retelling from Egypt to David: God's gifts, the people's ingratitude, his patience.
Tell the next generation, so they do not repeat it.
78: The nations have defiled your temple. "Do not remember our former sins. Help us, for the glory of your name."
79: "Shepherd of Israel, hear us." You brought a vine out of Egypt; why are its walls broken?
"Let your face shine, and we shall be saved."
80: If only my people would listen
A festival song. "Open your mouth wide and I will fill it." But my people did not listen.
God longs to feed his people with the finest wheat.
81: "How long will you judge unjustly? Defend the poor and the orphan."
Jesus quotes "You are gods" in John 10.
82: Nations plot to wipe out Israel.
That they may know that you alone are Most High.
83: How lovely is your dwelling place
"My soul longs for the courts of the Lord. One day in your courts is better than a thousand elsewhere."
The joy of being in God's house.
84: "Lord, you have blessed your land." Justice and peace have kissed.
An Advent psalm of salvation near at hand.
85: "Incline your ear, for I am poor and needy. You, Lord, are good and forgiving."
86: Glorious things are said of the city of God. Of every nation it will be said, "This one was born there."
The Church as mother of all peoples.
87: "My soul is full of troubles." You have taken friend and neighbour from me.
The only psalm with no turn to hope, yet it is still prayed to God.
88: "I will sing of the mercies of the Lord for ever." God swore an everlasting throne to David. But now the king is cast off: where is your former love?
Holding God to his promise in the dark.
89: Teach us to number our days
"Lord, you have been our refuge. A thousand years in your sight are like yesterday."
Attributed to Moses: human life is short, God eternal.
90: "He will give his angels charge over you. You shall not fear the terror of the night."
Prayed at Night Prayer. The devil quotes it to Jesus. (Psalm 91 in modern Bibles.)
91: It is good to give thanks
A psalm for the Sabbath. The just flourish like the palm tree and still bear fruit in old age.
92: "He is robed in majesty." Mightier than the thunder of great waters is the Lord.
Creation is firm because God reigns.
93: "How long shall the wicked triumph?" Does he who made the ear not hear?
94: "Let us kneel before the Lord who made us. Today, if you hear his voice, harden not your hearts."
95: "Tell his glory among the nations." Let the heavens rejoice.
The Lord comes to judge the earth.
96: Clouds and fire surround him; the mountains melt like wax.
97: All the ends of the earth
"Sing a new song, for he has done wonderful things." Let the rivers clap their hands.
98: The Lord reigns, enthroned on the cherubim. Moses, Aaron and Samuel called on him.
99: "Sing joyfully to God, all the earth. We are his people, the sheep of his pasture."
A short psalm of pure thanks.
100: "I will walk with blameless heart within my house."
A rule of life for anyone in authority.
101: "My days vanish like smoke." But you, Lord, remain for ever.
102: "He forgives all your sins. As far as east is from west, so far he removes our sins. As a father pities his children."
The great psalm of God's mercy. (Psalm 103 in modern Bibles.)
103: God stretches out the heavens, waters the hills, feeds every creature. "Send forth your Spirit, and they are created."
104: From Abraham through Joseph to the Exodus: "He remembered his covenant for ever."
105: The same history from the other side: "We have sinned like our fathers." Yet he heard their cry.
106: Four groups cry to the Lord: the lost, prisoners, the sick and sailors in a storm. He saves each.
"Give thanks to the Lord for his mercy."
107: "I will awake the dawn." Then a prayer for victory.
108: "In return for my love they accuse me." Strong curses follow.
A hard psalm. Acts applies part of it to Judas.
109: The Lord said to my Lord
"Sit at my right hand. You are a priest for ever, in the order of Melchizedek."
The psalm most quoted in the New Testament, about Christ as King and Priest. (Psalm 110 in modern Bibles.)
110: Great are the works of the Lord
"He has given food to those who fear him. He sent redemption to his people."
The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.
111: He is generous and lends, and his heart is steady.
"A light rises in the darkness for the upright."
112: He raises the poor from the dust
"From the rising of the sun to its setting, praised be the name of the Lord."
God stoops down to the lowly.
113: When Israel came out of Egypt
The sea fled and the mountains skipped. Idols have mouths and do not speak. "Not to us, Lord, but to your name give glory."
114: "He heard my voice. The cords of death surrounded me."
"I will walk before the Lord in the land of the living."
115: What shall I render to the Lord?
"I will take the chalice of salvation. Precious in the eyes of the Lord is the death of his saints."
Prayed in connection with the Eucharist.
116: Two verses that include the whole world.
117: "Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good." The rejected stone has become the cornerstone. "This is the day the Lord has made."
118: The longest psalm, 176 verses, each one about God's word. "Your word is a lamp to my feet."
A long meditation on loving God's will. (Psalm 119 in modern Bibles.)
119: "In my trouble I cried to the Lord." I am for peace; they are for war.
The first of fifteen pilgrim songs for going up to Jerusalem.
120: I lift up my eyes to the mountains
"My help comes from the Lord. He who keeps you will not sleep."
121: Let us go to the house of the Lord
"I rejoiced when they said to me." Pray for the peace of Jerusalem.
The joy of arriving for worship.
122: As servants watch their master's hand, so our eyes are on the Lord until he has mercy.
123: If the Lord had not been with us
We would have been swallowed alive. "Our soul has escaped like a bird from the snare."
"Our help is in the name of the Lord."
124: Those who trust in the Lord cannot be shaken. As mountains surround Jerusalem, the Lord surrounds his people.
125: "When the Lord brought back the captives, we were like men dreaming." They shall reap with joy.
126: Unless the Lord builds the house
The builders labour in vain. Children are a gift from the Lord.
127: "Blessed are all who fear the Lord." Your wife like a fruitful vine, your children like olive shoots around your table.
128: Often attacked since my youth, yet not overcome.
129: "If you, Lord, mark iniquities, who shall stand? But with you is forgiveness. My soul waits for the Lord."
The De profundis, prayed for the dead. (Psalm 130 in modern Bibles.)
130: "My heart is not proud." I have quieted my soul like a child with its mother.
131: David swore not to rest until he found a place for the Lord. God swore that his descendant would sit on the throne.
Read of Christ and of Mary, the new ark.
132: "How good and pleasant it is when brothers live together in unity."
Unity is a blessing, like precious oil.
133: "Bless the Lord, all you servants of the Lord, who stand by night in his house."
134: Praise the name of the Lord
He does whatever he pleases in heaven and on earth. He struck Egypt. Idols are silver and gold.
135: Creation, the Exodus and the gift of the land, each line answered, "for his mercy endures for ever".
136: "We sat and wept when we remembered Zion. How shall we sing the Lord's song in a foreign land?"
The exile's grief and loyalty. Its last verse is a cry of raw pain.
137: "On the day I called, you answered me."
"Do not forsake the work of your hands."
138: "You know when I sit and when I rise. Where can I flee from your presence? You knit me together in my mother's womb."
God knows us completely and made us with care.
139: Deliver me from the evil man
They sharpen their tongues like serpents.
"The Lord will maintain the cause of the poor."
140: "Let my prayer rise before you like incense. Set a guard over my mouth."
141: "I cry to the Lord with my voice. No one cares for my soul. You are my refuge."
Francis of Assisi prayed this as he died.
142: Teach me to do your will
"Do not enter into judgement with your servant. I stretch out my hands to you."
143: Blessed be the Lord, my rock
"Lord, what is man that you care for him?"
"Happy the people whose God is the Lord."
144: "The Lord is gracious and merciful. You open your hand and satisfy every living thing."
145: God keeps faith for ever: he feeds the hungry, frees prisoners, protects the stranger.
146: He builds up Jerusalem and counts the stars by name.
The God of the galaxies bends over the wounded.
147: He blesses your children, gives peace, sends his word like snow.
Thanks for God's word, given to his people.
148: Angels, sun, moon, sea monsters, mountains, kings and children: praise the Lord.
Everything that exists is called to worship.
149: "Let Israel rejoice in its Maker. The Lord takes delight in his people."
150: Let everything that breathes praise the Lord
Praise him with trumpet, harp, strings, pipes and cymbals.
The Psalter ends in pure praise.
